A refactor could silently lose the collided-row protection with no test failing.

findings.issue_text: [ADVISORY] No CLI-level test checks that roots() passes moved.Collisions to MigrateLegacyRows: migrate_test.go moved its row conflict to a different id, so dropping the argument would still pass every test. A refactor could silently lose the collided-row protection with no test failing.

[ADVISORY] While any collided run's row is deferred, the size stamp is never written, so every fsm command re-reads and parses the full legacy review ledger and re-emits legacy row-conflict warnings for as long as the collision lasts. An unresolved collision brings back the per-command legacy-ledger cost fixed earlier; collisions are rare and already warned on every command.

[ADVISORY] The new TestMigrateLegacyRowsSkipsCollidedRuns was inserted under the existing doc comment of TestMigrateLegacyRowsIsLenientAndRunsOnce, so that comment now sits above the collision test and the lenient test has none. Maintainers read the wrong rationale for the collision test and none for the lenient test.
